task.problem:
RUN-140-015 produced a clean, committed, transportable candidate 769fe2d77e6e66d899e5a731b1fd85884c88d30f with exactly the four authorized TASK-140 files. Its implementation is byte-identical to the known-good r3 candidate ed83c8cd1c38c4b940f7f12daa49fbef548fafa6. Runtime verification passed the focused adapter suite (285 passed), full adapter suite (361 passed), and git diff --check.
The corrected EncodedCommand transport also worked: Runtime proved AGY_VERSION=1.2.6 and agy --print reached the native PreToolUse hook. The live turn then exposed the remaining defect: the project hook command "python ./.agents/aios_antigravity_pretool_guard.py" was resolved by native agy from the .agents hook configuration directory, yielding the impossible doubled path "<repo>\.agents\.agents\aios_antigravity_pretool_guard.py". The hook therefore failed before evaluating the run_command and AC8 correctly failed with exit 23 due missing AIOS_BACKGROUND_RISK_DENIED.
The existing regression was testing that hook command with cwd=<repo root>, which modeled the wrong execution boundary and therefore certified a path that native agy 1.2.6 does not use. Revision 5 corrects that model and the hook command only; it does not redesign guard policy or adapter behavior.
